body:
Identity: Codex , posting as . I did not create or generate ; I first learned of it through this review call. I inspected it read-only and will not edit or stage it.

I agree with the owner disposition: retain it only as a composition sketch.

What it gets right is the coordinated-instrument intuition. The bird's-eye strip, readable-text region, inspector, global projection, feature tracks, and mapping face visibly share a focus. The episode/scene navigation and focus window are useful clues for the eventual instrument map.

It is not an acceptable scientific mockup in its current form:

1. The apparent Codex contains paraphrased or invented WOG prose and the graph promotes unsupported goals, elders, ghosts, locations, and causal claims without evidence/context/status. It needs exact admitted fixture output or a dominant SYNTHETIC / NOT MODEL OUTPUT watermark.
2. Numeric tracks and values (confidence, intensity, sentiment, tension, modality tracks, recall coverage/precision/misordering/omissions) have no units, reducer, window basis, coverage, missingness, provider, or receipt. Their polish currently implies measurements that are not present.
3. The recall face is categorical arrows, not the accepted matrix-first posterior view. It conceals multimodality and lacks Distorted facets, Unranked, abstention/unresolved mass, and distinct external states.
4. The screen presents too many peer panes at once. Exact prose is small and boxed in by dense controls. The product decision is docked observational text plus one replaceable projection and a persistent inspector; the bird's-eye view can remain a compact navigator, while Map, Feature Scale-Space, and Recall Mapping should not all demand primary attention simultaneously.
5. The zoom control appears optical. The required zoom changes typed representation over NarrativeLevel and SurfaceDetail, conserves Address and Codex focus, and exposes no SurfaceDetail control until storymodel4s compiles horizon-safe surface marks.
6. Colour and tiny text carry too much state. A revision needs non-colour type/status encodings, minimum readable type, keyboard/pick order, occlusion handling, and deterministic descent from every layout-only aggregate.

The new  and  draft deliberately encode those corrections: quiet split workspace, exact text as observation, one declared projection, receipted numerical features, matrix-first recall, semantic rather than optical zoom, and no display claim without evidence.
